title: Meeker Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Meeker wells have a 63 ft median depth; drilling and completing a typical well may cost $9,200-$16,700.
h1: What Meeker, Colorado Wells Are Really Like
intro_html:
Buying land around Meeker means looking closely at the well record, not just assuming water will be easy to find. Colorado DWR records show 362 permitted wells within 5 miles of town, with 206 recorded as constructed. Only 59 report a pump yield and 47 report a static water level, so the local data is useful but not complete.

Most permits are for domestic or household use, and the local records are dominated by unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers. Nearby wells can help set expectations, but they do not guarantee the result on a particular lot. Before buying, review the permit, construction report, water-right restrictions, septic layout and neighboring well performance.

sections.heading: Meeker well depths depend on the ground under the lot
sections.html:
Meeker wells have a median reported depth of 63 feet. The middle half runs from 38 to 155 feet, which means many drilling bids should be based on a relatively shallow hole, while still allowing for substantial variation. The 90th percentile is 280 feet, and the deepest recorded well reaches 1,220 feet.

Depth records show 59% of wells under 100 feet, 32% between 100 and 300 feet, 8% between 300 and 600 feet, and 1% above 600 feet. That spread matters when comparing bids. A quote built around the 63-foot median may not cover a difficult site. The local records identify 339 wells in unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers and 12 in alluvial aquifers, so the exact geology beneath the parcel remains important.

sections.heading: Most Meeker wells make useful water, but yield still varies
sections.html:
Among the 59 Meeker-area permits that report pump yield, the median is 12.0 gallons per minute. The middle half runs from 7.0 to 18.0 gallons per minute. That is generally a workable range for a household well, but the permit sample is limited and does not represent every constructed well.

Forty-six percent of reported wells produce 15 or more gallons per minute, while 44% fall between 5 and 15 gallons per minute. Ten percent are in the 1-to-5-gallon-per-minute range, and none of the reported wells are under 1 gallon per minute. A buyer should still ask for the actual well test, pump size, storage capacity and recovery behavior. A strong nearby well is encouraging evidence, not a guarantee for a new hole.

sections.heading: Water levels are shallow, with no simple long-term pattern
sections.html:
The median reported static water level near Meeker is 16 feet below the surface, with the middle half from 6 to 80 feet. A shallow static level can reduce pumping lift, but it does not by itself prove that the well will produce a strong flow. Static level, pumping level and recovery should be reviewed separately.

The decade figures do not show a steady decline. The median was 35 feet below the surface in the 1970s, 6 feet in the 2010s and 18 feet in the 2020s. Those measurements come from different wells and locations, so they are not a continuous monitoring record. Treat the series as local context rather than proof that the water table is rising or falling across Meeker.

sections.heading: Meeker’s permit history shows continuing well activity
sections.html:
Permit activity stretches from the 1950s through 2025. The records show 1 permit in the 1950s, 4 in the 1960s, 42 in the 1970s, 35 in the 1980s, 52 in the 1990s, 53 in the 2000s, 25 in the 2010s and 75 in the 2020s.

The most frequently listed drillers are Water Pump Supply & Service, Day, Travis, with 43 records; Water Pump Supply And Service, Day, Winfred C., with 34; and Shelton Drilling Corporation, Shelton, Wayne, with 15. These are permit-record names, not a recommendation or proof that they are available today. Ask for the construction report, casing and grout details, pump test and any work performed after the original permit.

sections.heading: A Meeker well may cost more than the drilling line item
sections.html:
For the mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground modeled around Meeker, the typical drilling rate is $50-$75 per foot. At the local median depth of 63 feet, the drilled hole works out to about $3,200-$4,700. That is only the hole, not a functioning water system.

The modeled finished-well cost is about $9,200-$16,700 after adding the pump, pressure tank, trenching and electrical work. A real bid can change with access, casing and grout requirements, pump setting, trench length, power availability and site conditions. Ask each contractor what is included, how extra footage is charged, and what happens if the hole has low yield or must be deepened.

sections.heading: Check water quality, dry-hole risk and the building layout
sections.html:
Local yield statistics are encouraging, but a new well can still miss the productive zone or produce water that needs treatment. The mapped area within about 10 miles includes 19 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 13 historic mine features and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. That does not establish contamination at a specific parcel, but it is a reason to test existing well water and investigate the site history.

Septic and well locations must be planned together. Confirm required setbacks, available space, slope, access for a rig, and room for a replacement septic area before finalizing a building site. Ask about casing, grout and sanitary protection, and have the finished water tested for the contaminants relevant to the parcel. A water-right review is also necessary, especially if the intended use goes beyond ordinary household needs.

sections.heading: Use nearby Meeker wells as evidence, not a promise
sections.html:
For a lot near Meeker, start with the Colorado DWR permit and construction records for the parcel and neighboring properties. Compare reported depths, aquifer descriptions, yields and static levels, then ask a local driller how those records relate to the exact ground at the site. The nearby records include shallow wells as well as much deeper exceptions, so one neighbor should not control the budget.

Before closing, make the well permit, pump test, water-quality results and septic feasibility part of the investigation. If building, price access, power, trenching, storage and the complete well system rather than drilling alone. Colorado exempt household-use wells still have limits and conditions, and an augmentation plan may be needed in an over-appropriated basin. Confirm the permitted use with Colorado DWR before relying on the water for a planned home, livestock or irrigation.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Meeker, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within 5 miles of Meeker is 63 feet, with the middle half from 38 to 155 feet. Fifty-nine percent are under 100 feet, but the 90th percentile is 280 feet and the deepest record is 1,220 feet. A nearby well helps with planning, but local geology can change the result on your lot.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Meeker?
faq.a: The modeled drilling rate around Meeker is $50-$75 per foot. At the 63-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $3,200-$4,700. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching and electrical work is estimated at $9,200-$16,700. Confirm what each bid includes and how extra footage or difficult access is charged.

faq.q: How much water do Meeker wells produce?
faq.a: Of the 59 local permits reporting pump yield, the median is 12.0 gallons per minute and the middle half is 7.0-18.0 gallons per minute. Forty-six percent report 15 or more gallons per minute. Ten percent report 1-5 gallons per minute, so a buyer should review the actual pump test rather than rely only on the area median.

faq.q: Is well water safe in Meeker, Colorado?
faq.a: Safety depends on the individual well and its location. Within about 10 miles, records show 19 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 13 historic mine features and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. Those locations do not prove a parcel is contaminated. Test the existing well, review site history and retest after ownership or construction changes.

faq.q: Do Meeker wells have a falling water table?
faq.a: The available decade medians do not show a steady decline. Reported depth to water was 35 feet in the 1970s, 6 feet in the 2010s and 18 feet in the 2020s. Because these are measurements from different wells and locations, they are not a continuous trend record. Use the individual well’s static and pumping levels for a property decision.
